structure_rules.rule: End-user installer packaging belongs to platform-desktop-app. Repository setup profiles remain in agent-platform install_mode.
structure_rules.reason: A developer setup and a distributed app installer have different audiences, risks, commands, and verification gates.

structure_rules.rule: The first desktop prototype should reuse workspace-monitor as the UI candidate unless research proves a separate UI is cheaper to maintain.
structure_rules.reason: The monitor already parses repository history and documents, so duplicating it would add product surface before the installer architecture is proven.

structure_rules.rule: Use Tauri v2/Rust as the selected first desktop shell architecture around workspace-monitor. Electron and Wails remain fallback candidates, but new implementation work should target the Tauri scaffold unless a recorded measurement or release blocker changes the decision.
structure_rules.reason: The long design review favored a smaller native shell with explicit command boundaries while preserving Python and Next.js ownership.

structure_rules.rule: Installers must not include real tokens, webhook URLs, browser cookies, private repository snapshots, or environment-specific secrets.
structure_rules.reason: A distributable app can leave the developer machine and must have a stronger privacy boundary than local setup scripts.

structure_rules.rule: A desktop build is not production-ready until signing, notarization where applicable, installer smoke tests, update policy, uninstall/rollback behavior, privacy review, and dependency/license review are complete.
structure_rules.reason: Installable software creates trust and recovery obligations that a local repository prototype does not.

structure_rules.rule: The desktop app may use external CLIs through explicit adapters, but it must not become a hard wrapper around one CLI.
structure_rules.reason: The platform should remain usable when optional CLIs are missing and should keep provider-specific command behavior outside the platform core.

structure_rules.rule: Desktop packaging and release planning must check platform-desktop-app/configs/user-flow-registry.json before implementation or production-readiness claims.
structure_rules.reason: A technically packaged app is not useful if first-run setup, workspace selection, optional capability deferral, task visibility, and recovery are not designed.

recommended_initial_path.summary: Build a Tauri v2 desktop shell that wraps the existing workspace-monitor static UI, keeps agent-platform as the Python layer, and treats Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, and other CLIs as optional adapters.
why: The repository already has web UI output in workspace-monitor.
A smaller desktop shell is preferable while the product boundary is still forming.
Tauri gives a clear Rust native boundary for future command scopes, sidecars, and signed updater work.
The platform goal is to configure multiple AI coding tools above a shared workspace platform, not wrap one CLI.

Wails becomes clearly better because the desktop backend becomes a Go-owned local service
Native packaging only proves enough because users prefer browser plus CLI instead of a shell

runtime_strategy.ui_strategy: Reuse workspace-monitor first, then add desktop-specific UI only when local desktop behavior needs it.
runtime_strategy.agent_runtime_strategy: Keep agent-platform as a Python-first platform layer. The desktop shell must not run agent logic in the renderer. Future execution must use a documented sidecar, local service, or explicit command adapter with lifecycle cleanup.
runtime_strategy.language_runtime_strategy: Use Rust/Tauri first for the desktop shell, Go first for a separate local daemon or operational CLI, Python for agent logic, and TypeScript/Next.js for the UI. Follow agent-platform/configs/runtime/language-decision-registry.json before changing this split.
runtime_strategy.cli_integration_strategy: Use external CLIs only through explicit adapter contracts from agent-platform/configs/integrations/cli-adapter-registry.json. Missing optional CLIs should disable only that capability and show setup guidance.
runtime_strategy.data_strategy: Read repository documents or generated snapshots through explicit user-selected workspace paths. Do not silently bundle private repository data.
runtime_strategy.settings_strategy: Store user settings separately from bundled defaults. Secrets must be environment variables, OS credential storage, or user-provided runtime input, not checked-in config.

security_privacy_rules: Do not bundle real webhook URLs, API keys, tokens, browser cookies, or private notes into installers.
Prefer explicit user workspace selection over scanning arbitrary folders.
Do not assume one external CLI is installed; use adapter capability checks and missing-CLI fallback guidance.
Before desktop-originated CLI execution, document command allowlists, workspace path allowlists, timeout, and secret redaction behavior.
Document any local server port, sidecar process, file-system permission, or network behavior before release.
Review generated snapshots before public or distributable builds.
